conventions.convention: Use the exp(-iωt) phasor convention and the ordered transverse basis (e_x,e_y) in a positively oriented SI laboratory chart. S3 = -2 Im Γ12.

At each fixed spatial point, Z is a measurable square-integrable complex two-component random vector. Γ = E[ZZ†] is uncentered; no zero-mean or joint spatial measurability assumption is imposed. Ensemble expectation is not identified with a time average.
The degree of polarization is defined only for S0 > 0. Unpolarized means S0 > 0 and Γ = (S0/2)I2. Stokes coordinates have squared electric-field units, rather than calibrated irradiance units.
A Jones transformation is a fixed deterministic dimensionless complex-linear map; it is not a random matrix correlated with the input.

Visibility uses two scalar beam channels on one probability space, the ideal ensemble mean-square response, and a full unit-circle phase sweep with Aζ = A2 + ζA1. It is defined when I1 + I2 > 0 and is not a finite-sample estimate.

load_bearing.statement: For each fixed ρ, a measurable square-integrable Zρ: Ξ → C² defines Γij(ρ) = E[Zi(ρ) conjugate(Zj(ρ))]. Define S0 = Γ11 + Γ22, S1 = Γ11 - Γ22, S2 = 2 Re Γ12, S3 = -2 Im Γ12, and, only when S0 > 0, P = sqrt(S1² + S2² + S3²)/S0. The same algebraic construction applies to two classical complex amplitudes of a common physical unit; beam-channel correlations are distinct from polarization components.

For measurable square-integrable Z: Ξ → C², Γ = E[ZZ†] is positive semidefinite and S0 ≥ 0, S0² ≥ S1² + S2² + S3². Equality in the second relation holds exactly when Γ = 0 or Γ has rank one. Consequently P ∈ [0,1] when S0 > 0 and is undefined when S0 = 0. A fixed deterministic dimensionless complex-linear map M transforms Γ to MΓM†.

For the stated common-ensemble square-integrable scalar two-beam model with a full unit-circle phase sweep, I(ζ) = I1 + I2 + 2 Re(ζΓ12). When I1 + I2 > 0, V = (Imax - Imin)/(Imax + Imin) = 2|Γ12|/(I1 + I2) ≤ 1.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite integrable expectations, linearity, positivity, and the elementary second-moment calculations throughout the batch.
The probability-space and square-integrable real-vector interface used to establish existence of coherency entries; its centered covariance is explicitly not substituted for Γ.
Complex conjugation, real and imaginary coordinates, and modulus in the coherency definition and visibility calculation.
Earlier deterministic transverse-wave polarization and exp(-iωt) conventions; the batch separately defines its ensemble polarization terminology.
Laboratory coordinate units, c, k0 = ω/c, and electric-field units.
Expectation as the probability-measure Lebesgue integral, through the expectation-linearity supplier.
The total-mass-one probability-space definition underlying the random-vector supplier.
The named inertial laboratory chart and its positively oriented Euclidean spatial basis, through the SI convention supplier.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier page, angular-spectrum definition, phase-multiplier lemma, and paraxial-error statement and proof against the consumer definition and remarks. Both sides use q = 2πξ, k0 = ω/c, 0 < δ < 1, and the positive axial branch. The consumer preserves the distinction between scalar L² propagation and exact vector plane modes, and explicitly declines to infer an aggregate ensemble or detector-error bound from the individual-mode longitudinal estimate.
